posts.title: What we lose when we dismiss the earth’s gifts and our neighbors
posts.description: In Melissa Harrison's new novel, everyday life for villagers in the fictional Welm Valley feels off kilter. A boy almost drowns in the river. A man almost falls off a roof. The birds are leaving. The story builds slowly with meaning that grabs on. Here's a review.

posts.title: Books for a book club
posts.description: New novels by Colm Tóibín, Yiyun Li, and Sebastian Faulks are among recommendations I gave at a lunchtime gathering, along with the winner of the 1965 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

posts.title: “His fiction is the world he lived in…”
posts.description: Breece D'J Pancake is a secret that shouldn't be a secret, an author who, decades ago, wrote about West Virginia. Here's how I discovered him, plus crime novels by Seichō Matsumoto, and Philippe Collin's new novel based on real events, "The Barman of the Ritz."
